original_value: The sustainability of regional water resources has important supporting data needed for establishing policies on the sustainable development of the social economy. The purpose of this paper is to propose an assessment method to accurately reflect the sustainability of regional water resources in various areas. The method is based on the relative entropy of the information entropy theory. The steps are as follows. Firstly, the pretreatment of the evaluation sample data is required, before the relative entropy of each standard evaluation sample and evaluation grade (SEG) is calculated to obtain the entropy weight of each evaluation index. After this, the entropy weighted comprehensive index (WCI) of the standard evaluation grade sample is obtained. The function relation between WCI and SEG can be fitted by the cubic polynomial to construct the evaluation function. Using the above steps, a generalized entropy method (GEM) for the sustainable assessment of regional water resources is established and it is used to evaluate the sustainability of water resources in the Pingba and Huai River areas in China. The results show that the proposed GEM model can accurately reflect the sustainable water resources in the two regions. Compared with the other evaluation models, such as the Shepherd method, Artificial Neural Network and Fuzzy comprehensive evaluation, the GEM model has larger differences in its evaluation results, which are more reasonable. Thus, the proposed GEM model can provide scientific data support for coordinating the relationship between the sustainable development and utilization of regional water resources in order to improve the development of regional population, society and economy.

result.paraphrase: Regional water-resource sustainability provides key supporting data for policy making on the sustainable development of the social economy. This paper proposes an evaluation approach designed to accurately capture sustainability in different regions. Based on the relative entropy from information entropy theory, the method proceeds as follows: first, the evaluation sample data are preprocessed, then the relative entropy of each standard evaluation sample and evaluation grade (SEG) is calculated to derive the entropy weight of each index. Next, the entropy weighted comprehensive index (WCI) of the standard evaluation grade sample is obtained. The relationship between WCI and SEG is then fitted with a cubic polynomial to build the evaluation function. Following these steps, a generalized entropy method (GEM) for assessing the sustainability of regional water resources is established and applied to the Pingba and Huai River areas in China. The results indicate that the proposed GEM model can accurately represent the sustainable status of water resources in both regions. Compared with other evaluation models, including the Shepherd method, Artificial Neural Network, and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation, the GEM model produces more distinct and more reasonable evaluation results. Therefore, the proposed GEM model can offer scientific data support for coordinating the sustainable development and utilization of regional water resources and for improving regional population, social, and economic development.
